items.q: Lan: Where's Nam? / Mai: He ______ dumplings in the kitchen since noon.
items.vi: Lan: Nam đâu rồi? / Mai: Cậu ấy gói bánh trong bếp từ trưa tới giờ.
items.explanation:
Since noon + an action still going on now ("Where's Nam?" – he is still in the kitchen) calls for the present perfect continuous has been making.
✗ makes — present simple states a habit, not an action running from noon until now; ✗ is making — present continuous cannot take since + a starting point; ✗ made — past simple means the action is finished, but he is still there.

items.q: I still ______ Nam fifty thousand dong for the bánh mì he bought me yesterday.
items.vi: Tôi vẫn còn nợ Nam năm mươi nghìn tiền ổ bánh mì cậu ấy mua cho tôi hôm qua.
items.explanation:
Owe someone money = still have to pay it back, which fits still and for the bánh mì he bought me.
✗ own — possess something (you cannot "own Nam money"); ✗ lend — give money OUT for a time, the opposite direction; ✗ keep — hold on to something; it does not take a person + a sum like this.

items.q: Lan: Sorry, I'm an hour late for the dumpling class! / Nam: Well, ______.
items.vi: Lan: Xin lỗi, mình đến lớp gói bánh trễ cả tiếng! / Nam: Thôi, trễ còn hơn không.
items.explanation:
Lan apologises for being an hour late, and Nam forgives her: better late than never = arriving late is still better than not coming at all.
✗ better safe than sorry — take precautions to avoid risk; ✗ easier said than done — a plan is harder to do than to talk about; ✗ no pain, no gain — you must work hard to get results. None of these answers an apology for lateness.

items.q: Lan ______ a photo of the lantern display and sent it to her cousin in Da Nang.
items.vi: Lan chụp một tấm ảnh gian trưng bày lồng đèn rồi gửi cho em họ ở Đà Nẵng.
items.explanation:
The fixed collocation is take a photo; the past tense took matches sent.
✗ made — you make a cake or a mistake, not a photo; ✗ did — do goes with homework, the dishes, not a photo; ✗ got — get a photo = receive one, but Lan is the one photographing the display and sending it.

items.q: Everyone in our street ______ to buy lanterns for the Mid-Autumn party.
items.vi: Cả xóm tôi góp tiền mua lồng đèn cho buổi tiệc Trung thu.
items.explanation:
Everyone paying towards lanterns for the party = a shared cost, so chipped in (each person gives some money).
✗ dropped in — make a short, casual visit; ✗ chipped away — remove something bit by bit, and it takes at not to; ✗ gave in — surrender or stop resisting.

items.q: Lan: The bánh chưng is burnt! / Nam: You ______ the heat on so high.
items.vi: Lan: Bánh chưng bị khét rồi! / Nam: Đáng lẽ cậu không nên để lửa to như thế.
items.explanation:
The bánh chưng is burnt, so Nam criticises a past mistake: shouldn't have + past participle = you did it, and it was wrong.
✗ needn't have left — it was unnecessary, not a mistake; ✗ couldn't have left — a deduction that it was impossible, but she clearly did leave it high; ✗ mustn't have left — English uses can't have for a negative past deduction; mustn't have is not a standard form here.

items.q: We can't ______ to eat out every night, so I cook at home most days.
items.vi: Nhà tôi không đủ tiền ăn ngoài mỗi tối, nên hầu như ngày nào tôi cũng nấu ở nhà.
items.explanation:
Can't afford to + verb = not have enough money to do it, which explains so I cook at home.
✗ pay — pay needs an amount or a person (pay $10 / pay the waiter), not to eat; ✗ spend — spend money/time on something, not spend to eat; ✗ cost — a thing costs money; a person cannot be the subject of cost like this.

items.q: The town ______ my grandparents live is famous for its floating market.
items.vi: Thị trấn nơi ông bà tôi sống nổi tiếng với chợ nổi.
items.explanation:
After the place noun the town, the clause my grandparents live is already complete (subject + verb), so it needs the relative adverb where (= in which).
✗ which — a relative pronoun must be the subject or object of the clause; here it would need in which; ✗ that — same problem, and that cannot follow a preposition; ✗ who — only for people, and town is a place.

items.q: This time next week we ______ mooncakes at the Mid-Autumn fair.
items.vi: Giờ này tuần sau chúng ta sẽ đang ăn bánh trung thu ở hội chợ Trung thu.
items.explanation:
This time next week pictures an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous will be eating.
✗ are eating — present continuous is for now or a fixed arrangement, not a scene at a future moment; ✗ will have eaten — future perfect means finished BEFORE that time, but we will be in the middle of eating; ✗ eat — present simple only works for timetables (the fair opens at 6).

items.q: If we don't hurry, we'll ______ the last bus home.
items.vi: Nếu không nhanh lên, chúng ta sẽ lỡ chuyến xe buýt cuối về nhà.
items.explanation:
You miss a bus, train or plane = arrive too late to catch it, which fits if we don't hurry.
✗ lose — you lose a thing you owned (keys, a match), not a bus you never boarded; ✗ drop — let something fall; ✗ fail — fail an exam or fail to do something; it takes to + verb, not the bus.

items.q: My mother is very proud ______ her recipe for fish sauce dressing.
items.vi: Mẹ tôi rất tự hào về công thức nước mắm chấm của bà.
items.explanation:
The adjective proud takes the fixed preposition of: proud of someone/something.
✗ on — not used after proud (on follows keen, depend); ✗ with — goes with pleased / satisfied with, not proud; ✗ about — goes with happy / worried about; proud never takes it.

items.q: Remember to ______ the cookery book to the library by Friday.
items.vi: Nhớ trả cuốn sách nấu ăn cho thư viện trước thứ Sáu nhé.
items.explanation:
To the library by Friday means giving the book BACK: return.
✗ borrow — take something for a while (you borrow FROM the library); ✗ lend — give your OWN thing to someone temporarily, but the book belongs to the library; ✗ rent — pay money to use a room, car or bike; library books are not rented.

items.q: Half the class ______ flu after eating ice cream in the rain at the fair.
items.vi: Nửa lớp bị cúm sau khi ăn kem dưới mưa ở hội chợ.
items.explanation:
Flu after ice cream in the rain = falling ill, so came down with (start to suffer from an illness).
✗ came up with — think of an idea or plan; ✗ put up with — tolerate something annoying; ✗ came across — find or meet by chance.

items.q: Wrapping bánh chưng takes ______ patience, so my grandmother starts early in the morning.
items.vi: Gói bánh chưng cần rất nhiều kiên nhẫn, nên bà tôi bắt đầu từ sáng sớm.
items.explanation:
Patience is an uncountable noun, so the quantifier must be one for uncountables: a great deal of (= a lot of).
✗ a large number of — only with plural countables (a large number of guests); ✗ a few — plural countables only, and "a few patience" is impossible; ✗ many — plural countables only; uncountables take much.

items.q: Nam keeps promising to help clean up after the festival, but ______.
options: every cloud has a silver lining
two heads are better than one
items.vi: Nam cứ hứa sẽ giúp dọn dẹp sau lễ hội, nhưng hành động mới nói lên tất cả.
items.explanation:
Keeps promising ... but contrasts words with (missing) deeds, so actions speak louder than words = what you do matters more than what you say.
✗ practice makes perfect — repeating a skill makes you good at it; ✗ every cloud has a silver lining — something good comes out of bad luck; ✗ two heads are better than one — working together beats working alone.

items.q: We're all looking forward ______ the lantern parade next week.
items.vi: Tất cả chúng tôi đều mong được xem lễ rước đèn tuần tới.
items.explanation:
In look forward to, to is a preposition, not part of an infinitive, so it must be followed by a gerund: to seeing.
✗ to see — an infinitive after a preposition is impossible; ✗ seeing — drops the required to of the phrase look forward TO; ✗ see — a bare verb cannot follow look forward at all.

items.q: The restaurant will ______ your phở to your door within thirty minutes.
items.vi: Nhà hàng sẽ giao phở tới tận cửa nhà bạn trong vòng ba mươi phút.
items.explanation:
To your door within thirty minutes describes bringing goods to a customer's home: deliver.
✗ order — ask for food; the customer orders, not the restaurant; ✗ serve — bring food to the table inside the restaurant, not to your door; ✗ receive — get something; the customer receives the phở, the restaurant does not.

items.q: You won't find a seat at the night market food stalls ______ you get there before six.
items.vi: Bạn sẽ không kiếm được chỗ ngồi ở các quầy ăn chợ đêm trừ khi bạn tới đó trước sáu giờ.
items.explanation:
Unless = if ... not: you won't find a seat if you do not get there before six, which is the logical warning.
✗ if — gives the reverse meaning (arriving early would cost you a seat); ✗ although — shows contrast between two facts, not a condition; ✗ so that — shows purpose and would need a modal (so that you can...).

items.q: Nam: Why weren't you at the parade? / Lan: Something ______ at home just as I was leaving.
items.vi: Nam: Sao cậu không đến xem diễu hành? / Lan: Có chuyện phát sinh ở nhà đúng lúc mình chuẩn bị đi.
items.explanation:
Just as I was leaving fixes the event at one finished moment in the past, so the past simple cropped up (= happened unexpectedly).
✗ has cropped up — present perfect cannot combine with a definite past moment like as I was leaving; ✗ crops up — present simple states a habit, not a single past event; ✗ is cropping up — present continuous is for something happening right now.

items.q: I wish I ______ how to make mooncakes as well as my grandmother does.
items.vi: Ước gì tôi biết làm bánh trung thu ngon như bà tôi.
items.explanation:
A wish about a PRESENT situation (as well as my grandmother does) uses wish + past simple: I wish I knew.
✗ know — a present form is never used after wish; ✗ had known — past perfect expresses regret about the PAST, but does shows the wish is about now; ✗ would know — wish + would is for someone else's annoying behaviour, not for the speaker's own knowledge.

items.q: Could you ______ the table while I fry the fish?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn giúp mẹ trong lúc mẹ chiên cá nhé?
items.explanation:
The fixed collocation is lay the table (also set the table) = put out plates and cutlery before a meal, which fits while I fry the fish.
✗ put — put needs a place (put the table by the wall); ✗ place — same as put: position an object somewhere; ✗ fix — repair or attach; nothing here is broken.

items.q: Red envelopes ______ to children on the first morning of Tet.
items.vi: Bao lì xì được trao cho trẻ em vào sáng mùng Một Tết.
items.explanation:
Red envelopes do not give, they are given, and on the first morning of Tet is a yearly custom, so present simple passive: are given (be + past participle).
✗ give — active; the envelopes would be doing the giving; ✗ are giving — active continuous, same problem, and a custom is not in progress now; ✗ given — a past participle alone has no auxiliary, so the sentence has no verb.

items.q: Can you ______ me a few minutes to explain the new bus route?
items.vi: Bạn có thể dành cho mình vài phút để giải thích tuyến xe buýt mới không?
items.explanation:
Spare someone a few minutes = give them a little of your time; the pattern is spare + person + time.
✗ share — divide something between people; you share food, not "share me a few minutes"; ✗ save — keep something for later; "save me a few minutes" would mean reduce the time I need, not give me time; ✗ spend — use time yourself; it never takes a person as its object.

items.q: Mai said she ______ the flower market the next morning to buy peach blossom.
items.vi: Mai nói sáng hôm sau cô ấy sẽ đi chợ hoa mua cành đào.
items.explanation:
Reporting verb in the past (said) + the next morning (the reported form of "tomorrow morning") means the tense shifts back: will visit → would visit.
✗ will visit — no backshift after said; ✗ visits — present simple states a habit and ignores the backshift; ✗ has visited — present perfect means already done, but the next morning is still in the future from her viewpoint.

items.q: The traffic in the city centre is ______ than it was five years ago.
items.vi: Giao thông ở trung tâm thành phố tệ hơn nhiều so với năm năm trước.
items.explanation:
Than needs a comparative; bad is irregular (worse), and far strengthens it: far worse than.
✗ more worse — a double comparative; worse already means more bad; ✗ much worst — worst is the superlative and cannot follow much or precede than; ✗ worst — superlative, used with the for three or more, not with than.
